title: Min and max in one pass
hints: `first` is a plain `int`; `rest` is a slice of the remaining arguments (possibly empty). `first` is both the smallest and the largest number seen so far.
Initialize with `lo, hi = first, first`, then `for _, n := range rest { ... }` and update `lo` or `hi` when `n` beats them.
Inside the loop: `if n < lo { lo = n }` and `if n > hi { hi = n }`. End with `return lo, hi` (or a naked `return`).
